policy: Eleven delta models checked against live Running Warehouse listings where available, otherwise the exact manufacturer's product page or Doctors of Running. Retailer men's/unisex US 9 measurements supersede the supplied CSV's mixed-size estimates. Manufacturer and reviewer measurement bases are disclosed. Recorded prices are snapshots, not stock guarantees. No hands-on ratings or invented specifications.

shoes.description: Lower-stack Hyperboost Pro daily trainer, distinct from Hyperboost Edge. Running Warehouse lists an 8.7 oz men's US 9 shoe and 38/32 mm stack. Its $169.95 price was observed on one US colorway; fit and performance are not independently tested here.

Fast road training shoe with dual-layer PEBA cushioning and a split Pebax plate, not a carbon plate. Running Warehouse lists an 8.4 oz men's US 9 shoe and 34/30 mm stack. Its first-sale date is uncertain across release calendars.

Women-specific road and everyday-movement shoe with FF LUXE cushioning and a 6 mm drop. ASICS launched it globally on September 1, 2026, not in October as the supplied release calendar suggested. ASICS quotes 7.4 oz without a comparable men's US 9 basis, so catalog weight and stack remain unpublished.

Max-cushion road shoe intended for relaxed runs, walking and recovery sessions. Running Warehouse's unisex men's US 9 listing is 10.1 oz with 47/39 mm stack; these measured figures replace the CSV's 10.51 oz and 48/40 mm claims. No recovery benefit is proven by the shoe alone.

Low-stack, foot-shaped road trainer for a more connected feel. Lems lists 24/22 mm stack, a 2 mm drop and 8.8 oz for a men's US 10 shoe, so its weight is not directly comparable to Running Warehouse men's US 9 measurements. ZENCELL blends EVA with 10% PEBA.

Foot-shaped road trainer with more cushioning and a rocker than ZenSpeed Lite. Lems lists 31/26 mm stack, a 5 mm drop and 9.4 oz for a men's US 10 shoe; compare its weight only with the same measurement size. ZENCELL blends EVA with 10% PEBA.

High-cushion road trainer combining nitrogen-infused PEBA Enerzy NXT+ with EVA-based Enerzy NXT. Running Warehouse's men's US 9 measurement is 10.3 oz and 46/40 mm stack, not the 47/41 mm preview values in the CSV.

Carbon-plated HyperFloat racing and workout shoe. Doctors of Running reports 7.4 oz for men's US 9 and an 8 mm drop; the brand has not published stack heights, so they remain blank. The $220 price is linked to Reebok's product listing in the source review.

Accommodating, orthotic-friendly road trainer with softer PWRRUN cushioning and a stable, straight-lasted platform. Saucony lists it at $155; multiple specialist retailers report an 8 mm drop. Conflicting stack and weight figures are left unpublished until a comparable measurement is confirmed.

Road-racing shoe with Hyper Burst Pro supercritical ATPU foam and a carbon-infused TPU Quantum Plate, not an asserted full-carbon plate. Running Warehouse lists 6.0 oz for a men's US 9 shoe and 40/36 mm stack; the $224.95 price is a snapshot for one colorway.

Protective trail and hiking shoe with forefoot rock plate, abrasion-resistant mesh and gaiter attachment. Topo calls it a low-top hiker; Running Warehouse also lists it for technical trails. The men's US 9 listing is 11.2 oz with 33/28 mm stack. It is not a road trainer.

differences: Hyperboost Run has 38/32 mm measured stack and a 6 mm drop; the older Evo SL record has not been reverified on the same basis.
Hyperboost Run is positioned for regular mileage; verify fit and the older model's current listing before choosing.
comparisons.verdict: Different daily-training roles. Do not infer a faster shoe from foam names or historical catalog values; test both for the sessions you run most.

differences: Tempo 2 uses a split Pebax plate, not a carbon plate.
The Vanish Carbon 2 is a separate racing model with older, unverified measurements.
comparisons.verdict: Shortlist Tempo 2 for faster training and evaluate Vanish Carbon 2 only after checking its current source and fit. They are not consecutive versions.

differences: Bloomstride is designed specifically around women's fit and has a 6 mm drop.
Nimbus 28 is a max-cushion road trainer with Running Warehouse men's US 9 measurements; weights are not directly comparable.
comparisons.verdict: Choose by fit and desired cushioning role. The women-specific Bloomstride is not a replacement for Nimbus 28, and mixed measurement sizes cannot establish a weight winner.

differences: Gel Slowcush has 47/39 mm stack and a 10.1 oz unisex men's US 9 listing.
Nimbus 28 has 42/34 mm stack and a 9.6 oz men's US 9 listing; height and weight do not prove comfort or recovery benefit.
comparisons.verdict: Slowcush emphasizes very deep cushioning for relaxed outings; Nimbus 28 is a more conventional daily trainer. Try the fit and transition rather than assuming taller is better.

differences: Both manufacturer weights use men's US 10: Lite 8.8 oz, Plus 9.4 oz.
Lite has 24/22 mm stack and 2 mm drop; Plus has 31/26 mm stack and 5 mm drop.
comparisons.verdict: Lite favors a lower, more connected platform; Plus adds cushioning for longer everyday mileage. These are sibling models, not an upgrade sequence.

differences: Sky Prime is a new high-cushion PEBA/EVA model with 46/40 mm Running Warehouse stack.
Wave Sky 7 is a separate historical model whose recorded figures need source re-verification.
comparisons.verdict: Compare these as different Mizuno long-run options, not consecutive versions. Confirm fit and the older shoe's actual listing before interpreting a specification gap.

differences: SpeedShifter is a $220 carbon-plated race/workout model; its stack is not published in the specialist review.
Endorphin Pro 5 has a $239.95 recorded Running Warehouse listing and 39/31 mm stack; the source methods differ.
comparisons.verdict: Both merit a race-day try-on, but there is no measured performance winner. Rehearse the chosen pair before racing.

differences: Echelon 11 emphasizes an orthotic-friendly, straight-lasted fit and 8 mm reported drop.
Guide 19 is a different support platform with an older catalog record; do not treat it as an Echelon predecessor.
comparisons.verdict: Choose according to actual fit and support needs. Verify Guide 19's current specifications before drawing a numerical comparison.

differences: Aero Elite's source-checked men's US 9 figures are 6.0 oz and 40/36 mm stack.
Endorphin Elite 3 is a separate racing model whose catalog measurement basis has not been reverified.
comparisons.verdict: Both are race-oriented; neither has a defensible universal winner from the current evidence. Check fit, race-distance comfort and source dates.

differences: Traverse 2 is positioned as a protective trail/hiking shoe with a 5 mm drop and forefoot rock plate.
Lone Peak 8 is an older trail model with historical specifications; surface and protection needs matter more than brand.
comparisons.verdict: Choose for the actual trail terrain and fit. Traverse 2's hiking emphasis and the older Lone Peak record make a simple numerical winner misleading.

differences: Clifton 11 has a verified 43/35 mm stack and 8 mm listed drop.
Clifton 10 is a historical catalog record; compare its current retailer specification before attributing a change to the new version.
comparisons.verdict: A new version number alone is not an upgrade reason. Test Clifton 11 if your Clifton 10 fit or ride needs replacing, and compare source-matched measurements.

differences: Kayano 33 is source-checked at 41/33 mm and 10.4 oz men's US 9.
Kayano 31 is an older historical record; Kayano 32 is not present in this catalog.
comparisons.verdict: This skips one generation, so do not present it as a direct one-version upgrade. Compare support and fit, then verify the older record.

differences: Nimbus 28 is source-checked at 42/34 mm and 9.6 oz men's US 9.
Nimbus 27's older record is not reverified on the same basis.
comparisons.verdict: Use Nimbus 28 as a possible replacement if fit and comfort improve for you. Historical measurements do not prove a performance gain.

differences: Glycerin GTS 23's Running Warehouse measurement is 39/31 mm and 10.8 oz men's US 9.
GTS 22 is an older, unverified catalog record.
comparisons.verdict: Both are stability-oriented trainers; compare fit and support directly before upgrading, and recheck the older specification source.

differences: Pegasus Plus 2 is source-checked at 39/29 mm and 8.9 oz men's US 9.
The original Pegasus Plus record is historical and lacks a like-for-like verification date.
comparisons.verdict: Treat Plus 2 as a new option for responsive daily running, not an automatic replacement for a comfortable original pair.
